To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the study was successful in achieving a sufficient sample size of participants who completed COMIT and were available for analysis.

a 30-day dietary intervention with oils containing n-9 and n-6 fatty acids, or oils with a blend of n-9, n-6 fatty and n-3 fatty acids did not significantly change the plasma concentrations of total DHA and total EPA in volunteers with abdominal adiposity, compared to a diet with a blend of corn and safflower oils.

the consumption of diets containing different oils and oil blends, including canola oil, corn oil, flax oil, high oleate canola oil, and a safflower oil/corn oil blend, had different effects on plasma fatty acid concentrations, and that these changes were associated with the fatty acids present in the dietary oils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of n−3, n−6, and n−9 fatty acid containing oils and oil blends on CVD risks.
the effects of n−3, n−6, and n−9 fatty acids on the risk factors for cardiovascular diseases.
understanding the effects of different dietary fats on CVD risk factors, and the mechanisms by which these effects are mediated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the consumption of dietary oil blends containing n-3 fatty acids and n-6 fatty acids, in combination, or n-9 fatty and n-6 and/or n-3 fatty acid-containing oils, may be more beneficial than consuming oils with only n-6 fatty and/or n-9 fatty or n-3 fatty.
the study is well designed and executed, and that the data generated will be of value in the field.
the study is ongoing and that the results of the primary outcomes will be reported in due course.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study is a well-designed and conducted trial that has the potential to provide important information on the effects of different dietary oils on CVD risk factors.
we have demonstrated that the COMIT protocol is effective in recruiting participants and retaining them through the five phases of the trial.

this study was successful in recruiting a sufficient number of individuals with abdominal obesity to complete the trial and that the study will provide important data to enhance our understanding of the effect of different oils on cardiovascular disease risks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to conduct a dietary intervention trial in a large population with abdominal obesity, and to achieve excellent dietary adherence.
the COMIT study was able to be completed with a high level of participant retention, despite a number of challenges.
the use of canola oil in the diet is associated with lower levels of saturated fatty acids in the blood and that this is associated with lower blood pressure.
